name: Handling noisy and uncertain information
gist: Real-world data is messy with outliers and noise. How do optimization algorithms remain reliable when gradients are unreliable, data is heavy-tailed, or predictions are uncertain?
explain: In a perfect world, all your data is accurate and all your gradient estimates (the directions to move model settings) point exactly the right way. In reality, sensors malfunction, labels contain errors, and when you compute gradients on a small batch of examples, they point in random directions that average out only if you wait long enough. Some datasets have outliers—one bad example that is nothing like the rest. Financial data, medical measurements, and sensor readings all have this problem. When gradients are unreliable, algorithms might chase a false direction and waste computation, or they might freeze because every step looks equally bad.

The mathematical challenge is that standard algorithms assume gradients are unbiased (their average points the right way) and have bounded variance (they do not vary wildly). In heavy-tailed data or with outliers, both assumptions break. An outlier can pull the gradient in a completely wrong direction. Some problems have a few extremely large gradients that dominate the average, drowning out information from normal examples. Classical algorithms like gradient descent can spiral out of control or get stuck. Detecting and handling outliers requires extra steps and slows things down.

Papers address this with several tactics. Some use statistics that tolerate extremes: replace the mean gradient with the median or a trimmed mean that ignores extreme values so outliers do not distort the average. Others use adaptive learning rates that shrink automatically when a gradient looks suspicious, which means the algorithm takes smaller steps when it should not trust its direction. Some algorithms maintain a confidence level for each example, starting high and lowering it if that example consistently gives strange gradients, so it contributes less over time and does not mislead the model. Others use clipping: if a gradient is bigger than a threshold, scale it down so it does not dominate the average update. A few papers study when noise actually helps—sometimes random updates push the algorithm out of shallow local minima into better regions where it can find a better solution, which happens because noise jostles the algorithm forward, so the noise itself is useful if managed carefully. The pattern is: algorithms that work well when data is messy are algorithms that do not trust every signal equally.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Linear Regression with Block Lewis Weights
papers.contribution: Achieves (1+ε)-optimal solutions with improved complexity over interior point methods for moderate accuracy regimes.

papers.title: Efficient Distributionally Robust Assortment Optimization in MNL Bandits
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical analysis and establishes sample complexity bounds for all three robust MNL formulations.

papers.title: Gen-DFL: Decision-Focused Generative Learning for Robust Decision Making
papers.contribution: Theoretically achieves improved worst-case performance bounds compared to traditional DFL, empirically outperforms existing methods on various scheduling and logistics optimization problems.

papers.title: Improved Stochastic Optimization of LogSumExp
papers.contribution: Demonstrates advantages over existing baselines in DRO and continuous optimal transport problems through theoretical analysis and experiments.

papers.title: On the Provable Suboptimality of Momentum SGD in Nonstationary Stochastic Optimization
papers.contribution: Proves via minimax lower bounds that momentum's tracking penalty is not an artifact but an information-theoretic barrier, precisely delineating regimes where vanilla SGD provably outperforms accelerated variants.

papers.title: Prior-aware and Context-guided Group Sampling for Active Probabilistic Subsampling
papers.contribution: Outperforms A-DPS, DPS, and all other sampling methods on classification, image reconstruction, and segmentation tasks across MNIST, CIFAR-10, fastMRI, and AeroRIT datasets.

papers.title: Robust Learning via Nested Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.contribution: Empirical results on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that nested DRO consistently outperforms geometry-coupled DRO baselines, particularly under heavy-tailed contamination where preserving high-leverage structure is crucial

papers.title: Variable Clustering via Distributionally Robust Nodewise Regression
papers.contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on clustering tasks through a principled, data-driven approach for robust region selection.

papers.title: Bregman meets Lévy: Stochastic Mirror Descent with Heavy-Tailed Noise in Continuous and Discrete Time
papers.contribution: Nonetheless, despite this highly singular behavior, we show that LMF attains $\epsilon$-optimality within $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-p/(p-1)})$ time in the convex case, and within $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-1/(p-1)})$ time for (relatively) strongly convex ob

papers.title: Bulk-Calibrated Credal Ambiguity Sets: Fast, Tractable Decision Making under Out-of-Sample Contamination
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive robustness-accuracy trade-offs and efficient optimization times on heavy-tailed, geographically shifted, and demographically shifted tasks.

papers.title: DUET: Optimizing LLM Training Data Mixtures via Noisy Feedback from Unseen, Downstream Evaluation Tasks
papers.contribution: DUET converges to optimal training data mixture even without fine-grained data information, with substantial performance improvements over existing data selection methods in unseen-task settings.

papers.title: Diffusion-DFL: Decision-focused Diffusion Models for Stochastic Optimization
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in decision quality through end-to-end training with a lightweight score function estimator.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization via Generative Ambiguity Modeling
papers.contribution: GAS-DRO with diffusion model demonstrates superior out-of-distribution generalization in ML tasks.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Distributionally Robust Offline Contextual Pricing
papers.contribution: Improves regret bounds for continuous pricing under distribution shift with semiparametric efficiency under mild conditions.

papers.title: Finding Differentially Private Second Order Stationary Points in Stochastic Minimax Optimization
papers.contribution: Establishes high-probability guarantees for reaching approximate second-order stationary points with rates matching best known bounds for private first-order stationarity in both empirical-risk and population formulations.

papers.title: Generalizing Stochastic Smoothing for Differentiation and Gradient Estimation
papers.contribution: Empirical benchmarking of 6 distributions and up to 24 variance reduction strategies for differentiable sorting, ranking, shortest-paths, rendering, and cryo-electron tomography.

papers.title: Gradient Flow Sampler-based Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical insights into DRO optimization dynamics and recovers existing methods as special cases while offering new algorithmic variants.

papers.title: LS$^{2}$MC-GDA: A Smoothed Algorithm for Federated Stochastic Multi-Level Compositional Minimax Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves sample complexity O(κ³/² / Nε³) and communication complexity O(κ/ε²), substantially improving condition number dependency and achieving linear speedup with workers.

papers.title: LiMuon: Light and Fast Muon Optimizer for Large Models
papers.contribution: Achieve O(ε^-3) sample complexity for non-convex stochastic optimization with lower memory, demonstrated on Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and ViT models.

papers.title: Loss-Aware Distributionally Robust Optimization via Trainable Optimal Transport Ambiguity Sets
papers.contribution: Produces less conservative decisions with enforced distributional robustness validated through data-driven bootstrapping on portfolio and regression tasks.

papers.title: Minimizing Upper Confidence Bounds: A Data-Driven Framework for Stochastic Programming
papers.contribution: APUB provides asymptotically correct and consistent framework with practical solution methods (bootstrap approximation, L-shaped method) fortifying decisions against epistemic uncertainty.

papers.title: Non-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems
papers.contribution: SPF outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both performance and scalability on least-squares recovery and logistic regression under distribution drift.

papers.title: OVLR: Efficient, Scalable, and Robust Training via Output-Level Variance-Reduced Likelihood Ratio
papers.contribution: OVLR enables practical optimization of gradient-agnostic objectives on deep networks, staying competitive where BP provides gradients and enabling learning on hard objectives.

papers.title: PASO: Step Parallel Stochastic Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 21x reduction in GD steps and 4.5x wall-clock speedup on models like Llama-3.2-1B and diffusion models without quality loss.

papers.title: Reducing Per-Sample Harm in Stochastic Optimization
papers.contribution: The method reduces per-sample interference and improves generalization on image classification benchmarks with favorable scaling properties as model size or input grows.

papers.title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Hessian Approximation: A Single-Step Policy Optimization Lens
papers.contribution: Provides unbiased Hessian estimators with variance optimality guarantees and establishes convergence guarantees for the resulting curvature-aware ZO algorithm, validated empirically.

papers.title: Robust Bayesian Optimisation with Unbounded Corruptions
papers.contribution: Achieves sublinear regret in the presence of up to O(T^1/4) and O(T^1/7) corruptions with possibly infinite magnitude, with near-zero cost compared to standard GP-UCB without outliers.

papers.title: Robust Contextual Optimization with Missing Covariates
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms impute-then-optimize baselines in both out-of-sample performance and reliability across contextual decision-making tasks.

papers.title: SVRG and Beyond via Posterior Correction
papers.contribution: Provides first connection between SVRG and Bayesian methods, enabling development of novel Newton-like and Adam-like variants with Hessian corrections.

papers.title: Solving Stochastic Variational Inequalities without the Bounded Variance Assumption
papers.contribution: Achieves oracle complexity of O-tilde(epsilon^-4) for making expected residual norm less than epsilon, best-known for constrained VIs.

papers.title: Step-Size Stability in Stochastic Optimization: A Theoretical Perspective
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical evidence that adaptive methods like SPS and NGN are more robust than SGD, with bounds qualitatively mirroring actual performance across step sizes.

papers.title: Towards Fully Parameter-Free Stochastic Optimization: Grid Search with Self-Bounding Analysis
papers.contribution: Achieves fully parameter-free methods in non-convex and convex cases with near-optimal convergence rates up to logarithmic factors.
